title: Real-life graphs
examples: How do I know if something is speeding up on this graph?
What does the slope of the line tell me about the journey?
Can I use this graph to find the total distance traveled?

explain.say: Today we look at graphs showing movement. These are called distance-time graphs. The vertical axis shows distance in metres or kilometres. The horizontal axis shows time in seconds or hours.
If the line on the graph is flat, it means the object is not moving at all. The distance is not changing even though time passes. This shows zero speed.
If the line goes up steeply, the object is moving very fast. A steeper line means a faster speed. We calculate speed by finding the gradient of the line.
For a straight line, speed is constant. We find this speed by dividing the change in distance by the change in time. This is the formula for speed.
Consider a car travelling for ten seconds and moving twenty metres. The speed is twenty metres divided by ten seconds. This gives a speed of two metres per second.

faq.q: What does the gradient of the line represent on this graph?
faq.a: The gradient represents the speed of the object. It tells you how far the object moves over a certain amount of time.
asks: How do I find the speed from the graph?

faq.q: If the graph changes from a steep line to a flat line, what happened to the object?
faq.a: It means the object slowed down until it stopped completely. The speed dropped to zero at that point.
asks: What does a horizontal line mean?
What does it mean if the speed becomes zero?

faq.q: Can I calculate the total distance just by looking at the graph?
faq.a: Yes, the total distance is found by looking at the final point on the vertical axis. That is the total distance covered.
asks: Where is the total distance shown?
How do I read the total distance?

faq.q: What if the graph is made of two different straight lines?
faq.a: This means the object changed its speed at some point. You must calculate the speed for each straight section separately.
asks: How do I handle different speeds?

faq.q: Is the unit for speed always metres per second?
faq.a: No, the units depend on what you measure. If distance is in kilometres and time is in hours, the speed is in kilometres per hour.
asks: What are the units for speed?

facts: Distance-time graphs plot distance on the vertical axis and time on the horizontal axis.
The gradient of a distance-time graph represents the speed of the object.
A horizontal line on the graph means the object is stationary, or has zero speed.
Speed is calculated by dividing the change in distance by the change in time.

quiz.say: A graph goes from the origin to the point (5 seconds, 25 metres). What is the speed?
quiz.why: You divide the total distance, twenty-five metres, by the total time, five seconds.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you might subtract the numbers, but you must divide distance by time.
wrong.1: This is tempting because you might add the numbers, but adding them gives a meaningless result here.
wrong.2: This is tempting because you might multiply the numbers, but multiplication is not the correct operation for speed.

quiz.say: If a graph is flat at a certain time, what is the speed?
quiz.why: A flat line means the distance is not changing, so the speed must be zero.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you might not see a number, but a flat line specifically means zero speed.
wrong.1: This is tempting because the line is drawn, but a flat line indicates no movement, not maximum movement.
wrong.2: This is tempting because you might assume a default value, but the graph tells you the exact speed.

quiz.say: A journey covers 60 kilometres in 2 hours. What is the speed?
quiz.why: You divide the total distance, sixty kilometres, by the total time, two hours.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you might multiply the numbers, but you must divide distance by time.
wrong.1: This is tempting because you might subtract the numbers, but subtraction is not the correct operation here.
wrong.2: This is tempting because you might change the units incorrectly, but the units must match the given values.
